note: The strongest ICP fit in the batch on every axis. He co-owns a company with partners, freelances project management for two other firms and runs rental property upstate — 'already successful, owns their own business' is met several times over. Income is evidenced rather than assumed: a household paying $700 a month for his wife's trainer, a home gym built out with sauna, cold plunge and machines, a new Amex Platinum, and an unprompted ceiling of "if it's a couple grand, it's not a problem... if we're talking $10,000, $12,000" before the price was quoted. Neglected health is not merely met but stated as the thesis of his life: "I've accomplished and succeeded in so many things in life, um, except me. Physically" and "this is the one area I'm lacking." Good-to-great is explicit at 6.5 out of 10, wanting definition rather than rescue. And he is far from deconditioned — 188 lb at 5'11", trains three times a week, runs up to ten miles, twenty-five years of physical trade work behind him. If the stated ICP describes anyone, it describes this man. He did not close on the call, which is the useful finding: across this batch, ICP fit did not predict outcome in either direction — the two closes came from an employee software engineer under the stated age floor and a salaried accountant, while the two best-fitting prospects both deferred.
